solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 27's companion spent time in cell

indicators.note: time that is spent is used up and gone, so the letter for time leaves the word

parts.note: 27 across is the electron; its partner particle in the atom is the neutron

explanation.surface: A prisoner's cellmate served his sentence alongside him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spent' removes the T from the electron's companion particle; the result is a nerve cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron is a nerve cell, the basic unit of the nervous system.

clue.text: GI struggles with some sense of superiority

indicators.note: letters that struggle thrash about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American soldier battles with a superiority complex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggles' rearranges GI plus SOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoism is excessive self-regard, a feeling of being better than others.

clue.text: The others keep coach in control

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: the rest means the others
a coach is a railway carriage, part of a train; train also means to coach

explanation.surface: The remaining players keep the coach in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' is the container signal; 'coach' is the railway sense, not a sports trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is self-control, holding oneself in check.

clue.text: Move ornament across Spain a tiny distance

indicators.note: the scrambled letters stretch across the Spain letter, holding it within
moving the letters of the word puts them in a fresh order

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Shifting a decoration over Spain by only a fraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' rearranges ORNAMENT into NANOMTRE, and 'across' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanometre is a billionth of a metre, an extremely small length.

clue.text: One-time Liberal knight returned bookplate

parts.note: ex means former or one-time

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the title reads backwards

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: A former Liberal knight came back with a book label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns SIR into RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex libris, Latin for 'from the books of', is the label pasted in a book to show its owner.

clue.text: Consumer's objective sure to vary

parts.note: an objective is an aim or end

indicators.note: letters made to vary change their order

explanation.surface: A shopper's goal is sure to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to vary' rearranges SURE into USER; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The end user is the final consumer who actually uses a product.

clue.text: Jargon employed in recycling organisation

indicators.note: letters employed in the phrase are used inside it, sitting within the words

explanation.surface: Specialist terms used at a recycling business.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for specialist vocabulary or slang, much like jargon.

clue.text: Expert tours lake and promontory

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so the expert word goes round the lake letter

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A specialist travels around a lake and a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a steep cliff or headland, a kind of promontory.

clue.text: Did she redraft a sea bill to help Columbus?

definitions.text: Did she redraft a sea bill to help Columbus?

indicators.note: a draft rewritten has its contents reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Was it a queen who rewrote a maritime bill to aid the explorer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'redraft' rearranges A SEA BILL; the whole clue also describes the Spanish queen who funded Columbus's voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Isabella of Castile sponsored Christopher Columbus's 1492 expedition.

clue.text: Sweden collapsed or inwardly deteriorated

indicators.note: inwardly says the next word goes on the inside of the other letters
a collapsed structure falls into a jumble

explanation.surface: Sweden fell apart, or declined from within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' makes WSENED and 'inwardly' is the container signal; 'or' is a real letter piece, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Worsened means became worse, the same as deteriorated.

clue.text: Any ------ could make agony aunt sweet

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are what the two parts could make together when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; the dashes in the clue mark the missing word

explanation.surface: Any confection might turn an advice columnist sweet-natured.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: ANY plus the blank, rearranged, makes AGONY AUNT, so the blank holds A, G, O, U, N, T in some order.
explanation.definitionFit: Nougat is a chewy confection of sugar or honey with nuts.

clue.text: Religious retreat has rancid butter

indicators.note: something rancid has gone off, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: a butter is something that butts, such as a ram

explanation.surface: A spiritual retreat keeps butter that has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rancid' rearranges HAS into ASH. 'butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu spiritual hermitage or community retreat.

clue.text: Rebuild croft in bishopric without penalty

indicators.note: in places the rebuilt letters inside the bishopric word

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

indicators.note: rebuilding something reassembles its parts differently

explanation.surface: Restoring a smallholding in a diocese, with no fine to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebuild' makes COTFR and 'in' is the container signal. A croft is a small Scottish farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Scot-free means escaping without punishment or payment.

clue.text: Brown tried acting naturally at first

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Brown attempted to act in a natural way.
explanation.definitionFit: Tan is a light brown colour.

clue.text: Non-stop thrashing by Inter Milan

indicators.note: thrashing beats the letters about into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football team endures an endless beating from Inter Milan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrashing' rearranges BY INTER MILAN; 'thrashing' looks like a heavy football defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Interminably means endlessly, going on without stopping.

clue.text: These melt in desserts; they're melting now

indicators.note: in puts the melted letters inside the desserts word

parts.note: ices are frozen desserts

indicators.note: melting letters lose their shape and run into a new order

explanation.surface: These melt in puddings, and indeed they are thawing today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melt' makes SHEET and 'in' is the container signal; the definition points to polar ice loss under global warming.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice sheets in Greenland and Antarctica are shrinking with global warming.

clue.text: Change fencing masters in old school

indicators.note: fencing encloses ground, so the change word encloses the masters

parts.note: to alter is to change
MA is Master of Arts, so two masters give two of them

explanation.surface: Reform the fencing instructors at the old academy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' is the container signal and looks like the sport; masters gives two MAs, Master of Arts degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater is the school or university one formerly attended.

clue.text: Turn away a story about Etna exploding

indicators.note: about puts the story word around the scrambled letters

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib

indicators.note: an exploding mountain blows its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A tale about the Sicilian volcano erupting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploding' makes ENAT and 'about' is the container signal; Etna is the Sicilian volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate is to estrange someone, driving them away.

clue.text: Fool stupidly cremated Devon speciality

parts.note: a clot is a fool

indicators.note: something done stupidly is muddled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A fool foolishly cremated someone in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' rearranges CREMATED. Devon is a county in south-west England; 'Fool' also hints at the creamy pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotted cream, thick scalded cream, is a famous product of Devon.

clue.text: Get up? Got up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Did you get up? I did.
explanation.definitionFit: To tog up is to dress, so a get-up is an outfit and tog is to dress smartly.

clue.text: Get up in the middle of late procession

indicators.note: in puts the turned word inside the middle word

parts.note: the core is the middle of something

indicators.note: in a down entry, up reverses the word

explanation.surface: Rise in the midst of a recent parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is the turnaround in a down clue and 'in' the container signal. 'late' means dead, as in the late king.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortege is a funeral procession accompanying the deceased.

clue.text: Hug and fondle, having been smitten

indicators.note: smitten letters are struck and knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cuddle and a caress, from someone lovestruck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been smitten' rearranges FONDLE; 'smitten' reads as infatuated.
explanation.definitionFit: To enfold is to wrap in one's arms, as in a hug.

clue.text: Stylist resigned having exchanged letters

indicators.note: the word swaps letters around, here its first and last trading places

explanation.surface: A hairdresser quit after swapping letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the R and D at the ends of RESIGNED.
explanation.definitionFit: A designer creates styles, as in fashion or interiors.

clue.text: Forge bit of gold into bar

indicators.note: to forge metal is to beat it into a new shape
a bit of the word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Hammer a piece of gold into a block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' gives G from gold; 'Forge' rearranges G plus INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a bar of cast metal, especially gold.

clue.text: Harbour runs off east

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A port route heads off eastward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges RUNS into NURS. 'Harbour' looks like a port but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a grudge is to harbour it, keeping it alive in the mind.

clue.text: Putting up Home Office money in government

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for the Home Office, the UK interior ministry
M is short for money in economics, as in M1 money supply
G stands for government, as in G-man

explanation.surface: Raising Home Office funds within the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting up' means housing someone, not raising money.
explanation.definitionFit: To home an animal is to give it a place to live, the same as accommodating it.

clue.text: Old car set off on November 5

definitions.meaning: a loud firework let off on Guy Fawkes Night, Britain's fireworks night

explanation.definitionFit: Banger is British slang both for a clapped-out car and for a noisy firecracker.

clue.text: Small matter of slogan during Reagan campaign?

definitions.meaning: a rallying cry urging voters to choose Ronald Reagan, split as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as a two-word election slogan for Ronald Reagan.
explanation.definitionFit: The electron is a subatomic particle, a minute bit of matter.

clue.text: Is he impressed by baroque tea-set?

definitions.text: Is he impressed by baroque tea-set?

indicators.note: impressed means pressed into, so the pronoun is pressed into the other letters
baroque means ornate and irregular, so the letters are twisted

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Might a person of refined taste admire an ornate tea service?
explanation.walkthrough: 'baroque' makes AESTTE and 'impressed by' is the container signal. The whole clue describes such a person.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is someone highly appreciative of art and beauty.

clue.text: Head of state tried changing pace

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
changing the letters puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A national leader attempted a different speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of' takes the first letter and 'changing' makes TRIDE; 'pace' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a long step, so a pace.
